summary: Tested Excel import NaN fix (safe_str) end-to-end. Backend: created xlsx files with openpyxl containing empty cells and full column sets, imported via POST /api/import/loans-excel, verified stored docs via GET /api/loans. The 'nan' string bug is FIXED (no field returns 'nan'; empty cells -> '', empty Status -> 'Pending'). All 15 requested columns map correctly (customer_name, company_name, contact_no, bank, status, category, product, amount, sanction, disbursed, login_date, location, branch, executive_name, team_manager) plus month/group_month. NaN cleanup migration verified: 0 of 25 existing loans hold 'nan' in any field. UI: logged in as admin, MIS Board -> Import dialog -> month select -> file upload -> import worked; table renders empty cells as em-dash, no 'nan' anywhere. NEW BUGS FOUND (same root cause family, not fixed by safe_str): (1) blank date cells are stored as the literal string 'NaT' (pandas NaT is not a float, so safe_str falls through to str()); (2) numeric columns that contain any blank cell are coerced by pandas to float, so Contact No 9876543210 is stored/displayed as '9911001100.0' and Amount 5000000 as '5000000.0'; (3) date cells are stored as '2026-01-15 00:00:00' instead of a date-only string.

critical.issue: Numeric Excel columns with any blank cell are read as float64, so Contact No is stored as '9911001100.0' and Amount as '5000000.0' — phone numbers/amounts corrupted (visible in MIS table). safe_str should strip trailing '.0' for whole floats (e.g. if isinstance(val,float) and val.is_integer(): return str(int(val))).

minor.issue: Blank date cells stored as literal 'NaT' (login_date='NaT'). safe_str only checks isinstance(val,float) before pd.isna; use pd.isna(val) generically and also treat 'nat'/'none'/'nan' strings as empty. Migration v1_clean_nan_values also does not clean 'NaT'.
Populated date cells stored as '2026-01-15 00:00:00' (pandas Timestamp str) instead of date-only, inconsistent with manual entry format.

ui_bugs.issue: Imported Contact No displays as '9911001100.0' due to backend float coercion (frontend renders raw value)

issues: React a11y warning: Missing Description/aria-describedby for DialogContent (import + other dialogs)

action_items: Harden safe_str: use pd.isna(val) for all types (handles NaT/None), lowercase-check for 'nan'/'nat'/'none', and convert whole-number floats to int strings so Contact No/Amount are not '...0'
Format date-like values as date-only (e.g. val.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')) during import
Extend cleanup migration to also clean 'NaT' strings and strip trailing '.0' from contact_no/amount in existing imported records
critical_code_review_comments: safe_str() checks `isinstance(val, float) and pd.isna(val)` — pandas NaT and pd.NA are not floats, so they leak through as 'NaT'/'<NA>'. Use pd.isna(val) unguarded.
server.py is very large (>3300 lines); import logic and startup migrations should move to separate modules.

success_rate.backend: 75% (3/4 test cases pass; edge-case test fails on NaT/float coercion)
success_rate.frontend: 100% for the nan-display requirement (dash shown, no 'nan'); contact_no formatting defect present

seed_data_creation: Temporary loans imported under months Dec'99 / Dec'98 / Apr-2026 with TESTNAN_/TESTEDGE_/TESTUI_ prefixes — all deleted after testing (DB back to 25 loans)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest /app/backend/tests/test_excel_nan_import.py -p no:randomly. TestImportEdgeCases::test_blank_date_and_numeric_cells is the failing regression test for the NaT + float-coercion bugs; it should pass once safe_str is hardened. Tests self-clean via module fixture.
rca_of_the_issue: Original 'nan' bug is resolved by safe_str(). Residual issues stem from the same source: pandas dtype coercion. Blank cells in a date column produce pd.NaT (not a float) which bypasses safe_str's isinstance(float) guard and is stringified as 'NaT'; blank cells in an integer column upcast the column to float64 so ints render with a '.0' suffix.
